items.title: 67259_Big Chief Moore oral history interview
items.q: I had occasion to sit in quite a few times. I worked one night with them.

ctx.x: No. No, because it was 10¢ a dance and the girls charged so much a dance and in the sequence of dances they try to get more and the customers that are lined up on the other side, why they get a great big roll of dance tickets and they go over and dance with the girls.
Oh, I see. How about A. J. Piron, you played with him for a while? Tell us about -- he was a rather suave individual, wasn't he?

Oh, yeh, played beautiful fiddle. He had a nice little group on Bourbon Street and I had occasion to sit in quite a few times. I worked one night with them. A. J. Piron, I shall never forget him, as well as down the street was Fats Pichon, famous boggie-woggie piano player and also -- I can't think of it right now.
